attributes.law_screen: Screened the full core-screen set (30 records) plus index-form signature queries. APPLIED: claim.law.direct-global-member-flips-index-base-association.20260831.v1 -- this is the governing matrix and it both predicted my probe's failure and supplied the disposition. Its cell (2) (pointer LOCAL + raw offset `*(T*)(p + off + K)`) yields addi+x-form byte-for-byte identically to cell (1) (pointer LOCAL + member access), which is exactly what I measured: NEUTRAL. Its cell (4) (global SYMBOL + member access) is the only form reaching the target's add+displacement, but its PROCEDURE clause disqualifies this function: count the target's lis/addi pairs for the symbol first, and if the target caches ONE base and does per-access adds, the residual is rematerialize-vs-cache register allocation. I ran that screen on the target -- exactly one pair, `lis r3,@lbl_80250E00(ADDR16_HA)` at 0x4 and `addi r31,r3,@lbl_80250E00(ADDR16_LO)` at 0x20, with per-access `add r4,r31,rIdx` at 0x28, 0x138 and 0x164 -- so the conversion is the law's documented losing trade and was not spent. That law also states operand order/parenthesization is a DEAD axis for this residual, which is why no second respelling was probed. APPLIED: claim.law.offsetof-fused-immediate-counter.20260830.v1 and claim.law.offsetof-rename-preserves-protected-web.20260830.v1 -- supplied the exact probed form (offsetof in an addend position on the original raw pointer, no typed intermediate); confirmed neutral, consistent with both. SCREENED: claim.law.recomputed-index-array-form-safe.20260831.v2 -- its warning that the array form is NOT automatically closer to target, and that the target's own opcodes at the cluster decide, is what sent me to the base-association matrix rather than to a blind array/pointer flip. SCREENED, NOT APPLICABLE: the home-copy and inverted-guard laws (no mr residual, no equality chain).
attributes.mechanism: NAMED, and identical at all three clusters: the target forms the element address as `add rX,r31,rIdx` (cached pool base + scaled index) and spends the constant 244 as the load/store DISPLACEMENT (`stw r0,244(rX)` / `lwz r0,244(rX)`); our build instead folds 244 into the INDEX (`addi r0,rIdx,244`) and issues an indexed x-form (`stwx`/`lwzx`). MWCC canonicalizes base+index+K to base+(index+K) and discards written associativity for every base/access combination except a global SYMBOL reached through member access -- and that one reachable form is disqualified here by the target's single cached base materialization.
attributes.residual: three add/displacement-vs-addi/x-form clusters at @28-30, @138-140 and @164-16c, plus the register-numbering noise they cascade; classified rematerialize-vs-cache REGISTER_ONLY per the governing law's own procedure. Next work on this function should target its structural residuals (branch shape, declared-local count, spill set), which the law says are what actually drive MWCC's cost decision here.
